subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Branch Coverage
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Branch Coverage.

hook.text: An if-else has two branches: true and false. Your tests only trigger the true path. The false path? Untested.

buildup.text: Branch coverage measures whether every branch of every decision point (if, switch, loop) has been taken.

discovery.text: It's stronger than statement coverage because it forces both sides of every decision to be tested.

twist.text: 100% branch coverage still can't catch bugs in compound conditions like 'if (A && B)'—both could be true separately.

climax.text: Branch coverage is the most commonly required structural coverage level in industry standards like DO-178C.

punchline.text: Every decision, both directions. Branch coverage forces it.

quiz.question: How is branch coverage stronger than statement coverage?
options: It forces both sides of every decision to be tested
